title: Finite coefficient change for ordinary direct image
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], with
$k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$,
a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$
and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, an integer $n\geq1$, and the finite coefficient ring
$A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension].
Let $B$ be a commutative $A$-algebra finite as an $A$-module, with
its constant coefficient sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let
$T,X$ be finite-type $k$-schemes and let $f:T\to X$ be separated of
finite type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Let $K$ be a bounded
constructible complex of $A$-module sheaves on the small étale site
of $T$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], with finite Tor amplitude:
there are integers $a\leq b$ such that $\mathcal H^i(K\otimes_A^L M)=0$
for every $A$-module sheaf $M$ in degree zero and $i\notin[a,b]$
(the étale convention in [lem-sf-flat-model]). Write $K_B=K\otimes_A^L B$
for ordinary uncompleted étale derived extension of scalars, viewed in
$D(T_{\mathrm{et}},B)$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], whose underlying
$A$-complex is the derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Then the
canonical coefficient projection map
$$
c_{f,K}^{A\to B}:(Rf_{*,A}K)\otimes_A^L B
\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{*,B}(K_B)
$$
is an isomorphism in $D(X_{\mathrm{et}},B)$. It is defined by the
$B$-coefficient inverse-image/direct-image adjunction: its transpose is
the $B$-extension of the $A$-coefficient counit, after the canonical
pullback/scalar-extension identification
[lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Upon restriction
to $A$-coefficients [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], it is the projection
map [def-kun-projection-formula-map] followed by the canonical
restriction/direct-image comparison
[lem-sbc-canonical-restrict-scalars-functor-comparisons]. Use derived
étale direct images as in
[def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. It is natural in $K$. For separated
finite-type maps $T\xrightarrow{f}X\xrightarrow{g}Y$ of finite-type
$k$-schemes, the equality
$$
c_{gf,K}^{A\to B}
=Rg_{*,B}(c_{f,K}^{A\to B})\circ c_{g,Rf_{*,A}K}^{A\to B}
$$
holds after the canonical direct-image composition identifications
[lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition]. For a commutative $B$-algebra
$C$ finite as a $B$-module, with coefficient chain $A\to B\to C$, the equality
$$
c_{f,K}^{A\to C}
=c_{f,K_B}^{B\to C}\circ(c_{f,K}^{A\to B}\otimes_B^L C)
$$
holds after tensor reassociation; $c_{f,K_B}^{B\to C}$ denotes the
same counit construction over $B$, whether or not $B$ is itself a ring
$A_{E,m}$. Let $\nu_W:W_{\mathrm{proet}}\to
W_{\mathrm{et}}$ be the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]
for each scheme $W$, and put $K_{\mathrm{pro}}=\nu_T^*K$ and
$K_{\mathrm{pro},B}=\nu_T^*K_B$, with exact derived comparison pullback
[def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback]. The canonical pro-étale map
$$
(Rf^{\mathrm{pro}}_{*,A}K_{\mathrm{pro}})\otimes_A^L B
\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf^{\mathrm{pro}}_{*,B}(K_{\mathrm{pro},B})
$$
is also an isomorphism in $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$ and satisfies the
same naturality and coherence identities. Here the map is defined by
the analogous $B$-coefficient adjunction transpose, with pro-étale
direct images of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]
and pro-étale derived tensor of [def-weil-derived-tensor].

proof.text:
The coefficient datum [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] writes
$\ell=u\varpi_E^e$ in $\mathcal O_E$ with $e>0$: $\ell$ is nonzero
and has absolute value less than one, hence is a nonunit of this DVR.
For $er\geq n$, the integer $\ell^r$ annihilates $A$ and is invertible
in $k$, since $\ell\ne p$. By [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], choose
$d\geq0$ with $\dim T\leq d$ when $T$ is nonempty; one can use
$d=\dim T$. If $T$ is empty put $d=0$: every module sheaf on its
étale site is zero and its derived direct image is zero by
[def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. In either case
[lem-sf-etale-direct-image-vanishing] gives $\operatorname{UDV}(f,A;N)$
for $N=2d$, in the sense of [def-sf-uniform-direct-image-vanishing].
Applying [thm-sf-direct-image-tor-amplitude] to a Tor interval $[a,b]$
for $K$ gives bounded constructibility of $Rf_{*,A}K$ and its Tor
interval $[a,b+N]$. Thus it is an allowed input for the comparison for
$g$ in the composition clause.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph through the direct-image Tor-amplitude conclusion

proof.text:
The coefficient datum [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] says $A$
is a finite ring, hence Noetherian: an ideal is generated by its finite
set of elements. A finite generating set for $B$ gives a surjection
$A^r\to B$; its kernel is finite and therefore finitely generated, so
$B$ is finitely presented. Apply [lem-sf-projection-finite-constant]
with $M=B$ and the bound $N$ of Step 1. Its current statement
uses ordinary uncompleted étale tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor] and
the unbounded K-injective direct image and adjunction mate of
[def-kun-projection-formula-map]. On the bounded-below objects here
the K-injective formula is also the formula of
[def-weil-pbc-direct-image]; thus the same functor and same mate give
$$
(Rf_{*,A}K)\otimes_A^L B_X\xrightarrow{\sim}
Rf_{*,A}(K\otimes_A^L B_T).
$$
Here $B_T=f^*B_X$.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: finite presentation, projection comparison, and coefficient-category identification

proof.text:
Put $S_W^{A B}=-\otimes_A^L B$ as a functor
$D(W_{\mathrm{et}},A)\to D(W_{\mathrm{et}},B)$
[lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The derived adjunction $f_B^*\dashv Rf_{*,B}$ of
[def-kun-projection-formula-map] with $\Lambda=B$ (the ringed-topos form
[lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], specialized to the constant
ring $B$) defines a morphism in $D(X_{\mathrm{et}},B)$ by transposing
$$
f_B^* S_X^{A B}Rf_{*,A}K
\cong S_T^{A B}f_A^*Rf_{*,A}K
\xrightarrow{S_T^{A B}(\varepsilon^A_{f,K})}S_T^{A B}K.
$$
The first identification follows on K-flat models by applying
[lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to $f$; its scalar
balancing is $f^*(x\otimes b)\mapsto f^*x\otimes b$.
This is the stated coefficient map, constructed in the coefficient
category before any scalars are forgotten.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: finite presentation, projection comparison, and coefficient-category identification

proof.text:
By [lem-sf-flat-model]
choose a bounded flat
constructible model $P$ for $K$. A bounded complex of flat
sheaves is K-flat [lem-weil-pbc-independent-bounded-flat-kflat] (flatness in
the sense of preserving injections is tensor-flatness, as tensor is right
exact), so by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], clause (2), its termwise
scalar extension $P\otimes_A B$ represents $K_B$; it is bounded, so the bounded-below comparison
[lem-sbc-canonical-restrict-scalars-functor-comparisons] applies to it
and identifies the right side with $\operatorname{Res}_A^B Rf_{*,B}K_B$.
The counit identity of [lem-sbc-restrict-scalars-derived-adjunction-identities]
identifies the restriction of this coefficient map with the displayed
$A$-coefficient projection map. Hence it is invertible: restriction
keeps the underlying abelian cohomology sheaves, so the cone of the
coefficient map is zero when its restriction is zero.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: finite presentation, projection comparison, and coefficient-category identification

proof.text:
These models are constructible: on a common finite
refinement of the termwise stratifications each term is locally constant
with finite stalks; tensor with the finite module $B$ preserves this
property, and kernels and cokernels of maps of finite locally constant
sheaves remain finite locally constant. The $B$-terms are flat, since
$(P^i\otimes_A B)\otimes_B M=P^i\otimes_A M$ and restriction of scalars
preserves injections. Choose also the bounded flat constructible model $Q$ of
$Rf_{*,A}K$ supplied by Step 1 and [lem-sf-flat-model]. Then
$Q\otimes_A B$ is a bounded complex of flat constructible $B$-sheaves
by the termwise tensor and injection calculations just given. Its
isomorphism with $Rf_{*,B}K_B$ shows that output is bounded
constructible over $B$. For a further finite $B$-algebra $C$, the
$B$-coefficient projection theorem applies as well: $B$ is a finite ring,
and for a $B$-module sheaf the restriction comparison identifies its
derived direct image with that over $A$, giving the same bound $N$.
Thus the two-step comparisons are defined and invertible without
assuming that $K_B$ has finite Tor amplitude as an $A$-complex.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: finite presentation, projection comparison, and coefficient-category identification

proof.text:
For a coefficient ring $R$, write $F_f^R=f_R^*$,
$G_f^R=Rf_{*,R}$, and $\varepsilon_f^R:F_f^RG_f^R\to1$.
The adjunction and projection mate are those of
[def-kun-projection-formula-map]; the ringed-topos form is
[lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Write $S^{A B}$ for the
scalar-extension functor of Steps 3–5, with the scheme subscript suppressed.
The defining transpose of the coefficient map is precisely
$$
\varepsilon^B_{f,S^{A B}K}\circ F_f^B(c_{f,K}^{A\to B})
=S^{A B}(\varepsilon^A_{f,K}),
$$
after $F_f^BS^{A B}\cong S^{A B}F_f^A$.
This identity proves naturality in $K$ by the naturality of the counit
and the adjunction bijection.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph through the successive-quotient and composition compatibilities

proof.text:
Use the canonical direct-image composition of
[lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition]. Its adjunction is the pasted
adjunction: the composite Hom bijection sends $H\to G_g^RG_f^RK$
first to $F_g^RH\to G_f^RK$ and then to $F_f^RF_g^RH\to K$.
Thus the composite counit is
$\varepsilon^R_{f,K}\circ F_f^R(\varepsilon^R_{g,G_f^RK})$.
Take the $B$-coefficient $(gf)$-transpose of the two sides of the
composition identity. For the one-step map it is the $S^{A B}$-image
of this composite counit for $R=A$. For the successive map,
naturality of $\varepsilon_g^B$ moves $c_f$ past that counit, and the
defining transpose identity first for $c_g$ and then for $c_f$ gives
exactly
$$
S^{A B}F_f^AF_g^AG_g^AG_f^AK
\xrightarrow{S^{A B}(F_f^A\varepsilon^A_{g,G_f^AK})}
S^{A B}F_f^AG_f^AK
\xrightarrow{S^{A B}(\varepsilon^A_{f,K})}S^{A B}K.
$$
Injectivity of the $B$-adjunction bijection proves the equality.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph through the successive-quotient and composition compatibilities

proof.text:
For $A\to B\to C$, take the $C$-coefficient $f$-transpose.
Applying the defining identity to $c^{B\to C}_{f,K_B}$, followed by
naturality of the pullback/scalar-extension identification, makes the
transpose of the two-step map
$$
S^{B C}(\varepsilon^B_{f,K_B})\circ
S^{B C}F_f^B(c^{A\to B}_{f,K})
=S^{B C}S^{A B}(\varepsilon^A_{f,K})
=S^{A C}(\varepsilon^A_{f,K}).
$$
This is the transpose of $c^{A\to C}_{f,K}$. Here the canonical
reassociation $S^{B C}S^{A B}\cong S^{A C}$ is computed on the
flat models of Steps 3–5 by
$(x\otimes b)\otimes c\mapsto x\otimes\varphi(b)c$, with inverse
$x\otimes c\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes c$. These maps commute with
all differentials and with the pullback tensor identifications
[lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback].
Injectivity of the $C$-adjunction bijection gives the coefficient-chain
identity in $D(X_{\mathrm{et}},C)$. Restriction/counit compatibility
[lem-sbc-restrict-scalars-derived-adjunction-identities] identifies
these specified maps with their underlying projection mates, as in
Steps 3–5; no faithfulness of derived restriction is being assumed.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph through the successive-quotient and composition compatibilities

proof.text:
The morphism $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated (finite type and
separated). Let $\beta_{f,L}:\nu_X^*Rf_{*,A}L\xrightarrow{\sim}
Rf^{\mathrm{pro}}_{*,A}\nu_T^*L$ be
[prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image]. Its specific counit normalization
is [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. On the bounded
flat model $P$ of Steps 4–5, exactness
[lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact], preservation of flatness
[lem-exc-constant-inverse-image-flat], and the ordinary tensor comparison
[lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] give
$$
\nu_W^*(L\otimes_A^L B_W)
\cong(\nu_W^*L)\otimes_A^L B_W
$$
for $L=K$ on $W=T$ and $L=Rf_{*,A}K$ on $W=X$: apply the ordinary
comparison in each degree to a bounded flat model, which is K-flat on
$W_{\mathrm{et}}$ and whose termwise pullback is K-flat on
$W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-independent-bounded-flat-kflat], so both
derived tensors are computed termwise. In particular
$K_{\mathrm{pro},B}\cong K_{\mathrm{pro}}\otimes_A^L B$.
The resulting pro-étale comparison is the composite
$$
(Rf^{\mathrm{pro}}_{*,A}\nu_T^*K)\otimes_A^L B
\xrightarrow{\beta_{f,K}^{-1}\otimes1}
(\nu_X^*Rf_{*,A}K)\otimes_A^L B
\cong\nu_X^*((Rf_{*,A}K)\otimes_A^L B)
\xrightarrow{\nu_X^*c_{f,K}^{A\to B}}
\nu_X^*Rf_{*,B}K_B
\xrightarrow{\beta_{f,K_B}}Rf^{\mathrm{pro}}_{*,B}\nu_T^*K_B.
$$
All arrows are invertible; $B$ is finite, so the site-comparison theorem
also applies with $B$-coefficients. Restriction of scalars on the last
term is the exact comparison of
[lem-weil-proetale-direct-image-restriction-of-scalars].

To identify this
composite with the canonical coefficient projection map, take its
$B$-coefficient pro-étale $f$-transpose, using the adjunction of
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Derived extension of scalars
$S^{A B,p}$ is the functor of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] on
the pro-étale site. Its pullback comparison is
[lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Substitute the
counit normalization of $\beta$ for both coefficient rings. The
$B$-coefficient counit composed with the last $\beta_{f,K_B}$ becomes
$\nu_T^*\varepsilon^B_{f,K_B}$. The transpose identity of Step 6
then replaces the composite with $\nu_T^*c_f$ by
$S^{A B,p}(\nu_T^*\varepsilon^A_{f,K})$. Applying the $A$-coefficient
normalization to the first $\beta_{f,K}^{-1}$ turns this into
$S^{A B,p}(\varepsilon^{A,p}_{f,\nu_T^*K})$. This is the defining
$B$-transpose of the canonical pro-étale coefficient map, so the maps
agree in the $B$-coefficient category.

The same transpose computation proves coherence there. For composition,
the $B$-coefficient $(gf)$-transpose of both maps is
$$
S^{A B,p}(\varepsilon_f^{A,p})\circ
S^{A B,p}(F_f^{A,p}(\varepsilon_g^{A,p})),
$$
by the pasted Hom bijection, or by successively applying the two
defining transpose identities and counit naturality. For the coefficient
chain, the $C$-coefficient transpose is
$$
S^{B C,p}(\varepsilon^{B,p}_{f,K_{\mathrm{pro},B}})\circ
S^{B C,p}F_f^{B,p}(c_f^{A\to B})
=S^{B C,p}S^{A B,p}(\varepsilon^{A,p}_{f,K_{\mathrm{pro}}})
=S^{A C,p}(\varepsilon^{A,p}_{f,K_{\mathrm{pro}}}).
$$
The balancing maps are the termwise maps
$(x\otimes b)\otimes c\mapsto x\otimes\varphi(b)c$ of Step 8.
Thus the $B$- and $C$-adjunction bijections prove the two pro-étale
coherence identities. Naturality follows from the naturality of the
counits and the displayed comparisons.

Finally
[lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] gives the finite-Tor constructibility
of $K_{\mathrm{pro}}$ and the $A$-coefficient direct image; the bounded
constructible $B$-models of Steps 4–5 pull back to bounded constructible
models by exactness and by pulling back their finite locally constant
stratified descriptions. No comparison on arbitrary non-étale-origin
unbounded inputs is used.

The etale and pro-etale naturality clauses follow from componentwise uniqueness without faithfulness of scalar restriction. Form the naturality defect t. Naturality of the scalar unit, the geometric counits, and the restriction/pullback comparison shows its scalar-unit/counit composite is zero. Insert t into an off-diagonal entry of the biproduct of the source and target complexes. Adding this entry to the specified coefficient map preserves its defining equation, so uniqueness forces the entry to vanish. Projecting to that entry proves naturality. For the etale restriction/projection clause take the A-geometric transpose. The mate/counit identity for the canonical restriction/direct-image comparison and naturality of its inverse-image square turn the left side into the defining scalar-unit equation. Counit naturality identifies the right side. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection gives the equality. All other clauses retain the preceding proof plan.
